what: my reading of the variance still grids (the moment +0.40 s after the contact; I cannot play video in real time — judgements from the stills and each tile's measured label)
hard_bc70_seeds: 16 seeds of the same BC 70 player on the same 22 m/s pass: 6 kill it dead at the foot (IMMEDIATE, stable 0.23 s), 10 leave a heavier ball that needs a second touch (RECOVERY), with extra steps from 0.37 to 1.62 m and stable control from 0.62 to 1.03 s. No tile shows a ball flying away: the worst touch is a 1.6 m step and a second touch.
hard_bc99_seeds: 16 seeds at BC 99: every tile is the same picture — one touch, the ball dead at the foot, stable at 0.23 s. The variation is invisible at this scale (the 1000-seed maximum placement error is 0.07 m).
hard_seed2_ratings: One below-average draw (seed 2: a stiff, rebounding touch) at BC 30 → 99: the same mistake shrinks with the rating — a 3.38 m chase and stable control at 1.62 s at BC 30, 1.63 m / 1.04 s at 50, 1.14 m / 0.88 s at 60, 0.87 m / 0.78 s at 70, 0.43 m / 0.63 s at 80, and one clean touch at 90 and 99.
t120_bc70_seeds: 16 seeds of the same BC 70 half-turn at 120°: the actual first-touch arrow fans around the ideal one; 11 meet the ball on the exit line immediately, 5 need a correction of 0.27–0.40 m (ADJUSTED). None needs an extra touch with these seeds.
t120_seed4_ratings: One draw (seed 4) of the 120° half-turn at BC 30 → 99: the actual touch arrow closes on the ideal one with the rating; the correction to meet the ball is 0.70 m at BC 30, 0.42 at 50, 0.35 at 60 and 0.37 at 70 (ADJUSTED — 60 and 70 trade a slightly different meeting point), then 0.16 at 80, 0.09 at 90 and 0.02 at 99 (IMMEDIATE).
